info.title: UARP — Universal Agent Runtime Platform
info.description:
API for managing AI agents, runs, sessions, and supporting infrastructure.

Auth: bearer API key (`Authorization: Bearer uarp_<prefix>_<secret>`). Browser SSE/WebSocket clients that cannot set headers may pass the same key as `?token=<api_key>` query param or `uarp_auth_token` cookie.

Idempotency: every mutating `/api/v1/*` request accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header; replays within 24 h return the cached response with `X-Idempotency-Replayed: true`.

bearerAuth.description:
API key in `Authorization: Bearer uarp_<prefix8>_<secret32>` header.

Scope catalogue (from `requireScope(auth, ...)` calls in route handlers): `admin`, `agents:read`, `agents:write`, `api_keys:read`, `api_keys:write`, `billing:read`, `evaluations:read`, `evaluations:write`, `events:read`, `files:read`, `files:write`, `guardrails:read`, `guardrails:write`, `marketplace:invoke`, `marketplace:read`, `marketplace:write`, `memory:read`, `memory:write`, `notifications:read`, `notifications:write`, `read:analytics`, `runs:create`, `runs:read`, `search:read`, `sessions:read`, `sessions:write`, `tenants:write`, `users:read`, `users:write`, `webhooks:read`, `webhooks:write`.

An empty `[]` under `bearerAuth` in an operation `security` block means any authenticated key passes; explicit scope strings restrict to keys carrying that scope. Most `/admin/*` endpoints additionally require role `admin` (RBAC layer beyond scope).

queryTokenAuth.name: token
queryTokenAuth.description: Same API key passed via `?token=<uarp_<prefix>_<secret>>` query param. Used for SSE/WebSocket/file content endpoints that cannot set request headers from a browser. For `/runs/{runId}/events` and `/sessions/{sessionId}/events` the recommended flow is to mint a short-lived token via `POST /api/v1/auth/sse-tokens` (60 s TTL, scope-restricted).

cookieAuth.name: uarp_auth_token
cookieAuth.description: Same API key set as a cookie. Used by the builder web app and any HTML rendering endpoint behind same-origin auth.

webSocketProtocolAuth.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
webSocketProtocolAuth.description: WebSocket upgrade only: subprotocol of the form `uarp.<base64(api_key)>`. Used by `/api/v1/bridge/ws` and other WebSocket upgrade routes.

Error.description: RFC 9457 problem+json style error; correlationId for request tracing.

OpenAiError.description: Error envelope used by the OpenAI-compatible surface (`/v1/*`). Deliberately NOT RFC 9457: callers here are OpenAI SDKs pointed at this base URL, and they decode this shape.

message.description: Human-readable cause, including where an operator fixes it.

code.description: Machine-readable code. `embedding_unavailable` = no provider configured (501, permanent). `embedding_failed` = the configured provider did not answer (503, retryable).

mission.description: What the company exists to do.

CompanyUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /api/v1/companies/{id}`. Every field optional — send only what changes.

workers.description: Each entry REQUIRES `agent_id` — omitting it answers `422 workers.0.agent_id: Required`.

TeamUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /api/v1/teams/{teamId}`. Every field optional — send only what changes.

AgentUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /api/v1/agents/{agentId}`. Every field optional — an omitted field means NO CHANGE, not 'clear it'. `model` and `fallback_model` are accepted and ignored (see the model lockdown).

CustomerUpdate.description: Body for `PATCH /api/v1/commerce/customers/{id}`. Only the listed fields are applied; anything else in the body is ignored.

ProductUpdate.description: Body for `PATCH /api/v1/commerce/products/{id}`. Every field optional; unknown fields are dropped without error, so a typo answers 200 and changes nothing.

tools.description: Tool names the SPEC registered into the local runtime.

error.description: Failure detail when `status` is `failed` — artifact 404, SHA mismatch, capability conflict.

specs.description: SPECs installed on this agent, with version pin and granted permissions.

enabled.description: Soft-disable. false keeps the install history but skips injection.

auto_approve_tools.description: Tools this agent may call without a human-in-the-loop prompt.

approval_required_tools.description: Tool names requiring human approval before execution

built_in_tools.description: Built-in tool names enabled for this agent

knowledge_base_id.description: Deprecated in `packages/types/agent.ts:296`; kept for pre-migration records. Use `knowledge_base_ids`. Documenting only the singular is why a client reading this schema could link one base to an agent that supports several.

knowledge_base_ids.description: Every knowledge base linked to the agent. `search_kb` searches all of them by default.

visibility.description: Who can reach the agent. The publication screen is built on this field.

status.description: Governance state, distinct from a run's status.

tool_overrides.description: Per-tool trust, overriding the agent's default approval policy.

bridge.description: Present only on `GET /agents/{id}`, and only for a bridge agent. Computed at read time from the machines currently registered, never stored on the record.

AgentModelConfig.description: Model capabilities. Deliberately carries no provider or model identifier — see the model lockdown.

capabilities.description: Feature flags the client may branch on (e.g. `vision`, `tool_calls`, `streaming`). Absent when the platform has published none.

AgentModelConfigInput.description: Accepted and IGNORED. The platform default is applied on create and preserved on update, so sending this changes nothing. Kept so existing clients do not start failing validation.

team_run_id.description: Team run ID if part of a team execution

fork_point_run_id.description: The run this branch forked after. Empty when the session had no runs yet.
Defaults to the session's most recent run.

parent_branch_id.description: Defaults to the session's active branch.

name.description: Defaults to `branch-<first 8 characters of the branch id>`.

team_id.description: Team ID if session belongs to a team

queue_mode.description: How to handle concurrent runs in this session

model_override.description: Per-conversation model override (in-chat model switcher). When set, runs in this session resolve their LLM from this config instead of the agent's default. Absent → agent default.

tool_calls.description: Persisted on assistant entries when the run executed tools. Reload re-paints these blocks underneath the assistant turn (matches what the SSE stream renders during the live run).

thinking.description: Reasoning / thinking content (DeepSeek `reasoning_content`, Anthropic extended thinking, GLM/Qwen `<think>` blocks). Persisted on assistant entries so reload re-paints the Thinking section above the assistant text.

AgentAnalyticsSummary.description: Output of summariseAgents (analytics.ts) — same shape for /admin/analytics/agents and /analytics/agents (tenant-scoped).

rule.description: The new rule, for `add` and `modify`. Absent on `remove`.

approved_by.description: The founder, or the consensus that carried it.

scope.description: Who the rule binds. The document previously listed `global`/`tenant`/`agent`, none of which the server has ever emitted.

scope_targets.description: Agent ids, team ids or role names, depending on `scope`. Absent for `all_agents`.

action.description: The action the rule governs, e.g. `modify_constitution`.

obligated_action.description: For `requirement` rules: the action that must be performed.

immutable.description: Genesis rules cannot be amended or removed.

priority.description: Conflict resolution — higher wins. Defaults to 0.

seq.description: Monotonic position in the tenant's chain.

prev_hash.description: Hash of the preceding entry. Null only for the genesis entry.

UsageSummary.description: Tenant usage for one billing period. Flat — the counters are top-level, not nested under a `usage` object.

total_cost.description: What the tenant is billed, in USD.

provider_cost.description: What the upstream providers charged, in USD.

code.description: The value delivered in the callback fragment.

code_verifier.description: The secret whose SHA-256, base64url-encoded, was sent as `app_code_challenge` when the flow started. It never leaves the app, which is what makes an intercepted code worthless.

config.description: The full agent configuration as it stood at this version. Shape follows `Agent`; not pinned here so the two cannot drift.

seq.description: Global sequence of the newest ledger entry across ALL tenants — not the newest entry in the accompanying page. Measured 2026-08-20: `head.seq` was 6698 while the last visible entry was 6697, and the gap is another tenant's row. A client must not use this to decide whether it holds the latest page.

first_invalid_seq.description: Sequence of the first entry that failed verification. Absent when `valid` is true.

issued_by.description: `ambassador_id` of the human who issued it.

Schedule.description: Cron-driven recurring run config attached to an agent (PUT /agents/{id}/schedule).

PermissionSet.description: Per-agent capability envelope. Invariant: PermissionSet(child) ⊆ PermissionSet(parent).

chain.description: Full chain from root to this agent.

child_budget_ratio.description: Child agent gets at most this fraction of parent's budget.

DesignRequest.description: Governance-builder request to design a new agent (packages/governance/builder-flow.ts).

proposal_id.description: Set once the request enters a vote.

spawned_agent_id.description: Set once the approved design has been created.

ImprovementProposal.description: Self-improvement proposal — multi-stage state machine (proposed → arbiter_review → voting → sandbox_testing → approved → applied | rejected at any step).

TeamWorkerPermissions.description: What a worker may do inside a team run.

tools.description: Tool names this worker may invoke. Defaults to the agent's own allowed_tools.

TeamWorkerExternalA2A.description: Delegate this worker to another platform over the A2A protocol.

TeamWorker.description: An agent acting in a team, with a role and permissions.

ValidationCriterion.description: One rubric line for LLM-as-judge validation.

ValidationPolicy.description: Optional gate scoring worker outputs before synthesis.

validator_agent_id.description: Dedicated validator; omitted means the supervisor judges its own workers.

auto_revise.description: Re-run the workers with the validator's feedback when a round fails, up to `max_revision_rounds`. Defaults to true — the server treats only an explicit `false` as off.

selective.description: Re-run only the workers whose output failed, rather than the whole round. Defaults to false.

TeamPolicies.description: Limits and failure handling for a team run.

on_worker_failure.description: Applied by the auto_dispatch supervisor. Under tool_driven the failure is returned to the supervisor as a tool result instead, and this policy does not run.

max_concurrency.description: Concurrent worker runs in a fan-out (default 8).

TeamSwarmConfig.description: Swarm topology: who starts, and how context travels on handoff.

TeamObjectiveBudget.description: Ceiling for a goal-driven team's pursuit of its objective.

TeamGoalConfig.description: Goal-driven topology: the objective, the review cadence, the budget.

RiskClassification.description: EU AI Act (Article 9) classification for an agent.

assessor.description: Key ID or user ID of whoever classified.

Guardrail.description: A webhook called before or after a run to allow, redact or block it.

ApiKeySummary.description: An API key as listed. The secret is shown once, at creation, and never here.

LLMProvider.description: An LLM provider the platform knows about, and whether a key is configured.

Program.description: An ordered curriculum an agent delivers.

McpServer.description: An MCP server as returned. `env` and `env_encrypted` are stripped; only the COUNT is disclosed.

env_count.description: How many env vars are set. The values are never returned.

capabilities.description: Tool names and resource URIs discovered from the server.

McpTransport.description: `stdio` is blocked in production unless UARP_ALLOW_MCP_STDIO=true.

connect_error.description: Set when the record saved but the session could not be reconnected. This is the only field distinguishing 'saved' from 'saved and working', and it arrives on a 200.

Company.description: Autonomous agent company — strategist + teams pursuing strategic goals.

priority.description: UI surface routing; defaults to `info` when omitted.

dedup_key.description: Notifications sharing a dedup_key collapse in the bell with a count badge.

ContentReportInput.description: An abuse/moderation report. Same body shape for the authenticated and anonymous endpoints.

reason.description: Closed vocabulary — unknown values are rejected with 422. `self_harm` raises the resulting operator notification to critical priority.

details.description: Optional free-text note from the reporter.

tenant_id.description: Tenant that owns the reported content — the queue this report lands in.

reporter_fingerprint.description: Truncated SHA-256 of the reporter's IP. Never the raw address; enough to spot one source flooding the queue.

Integration.description: OAuth/API integration record (Slack, GitHub, Linear, etc.).

config.description: Connector settings. Secrets are replaced with `<redacted>`.

status.description: `active` is what the server sends for a working integration; the documented `connected` was never emitted.

assigned_agent_ids.description: Agents allowed to use this integration. Present on the live record and read by 7 files in the web; the document omitted it, so a generated client could not tell which agents an integration serves.

key_preview.description: Last 4 chars only; full key never returned.

status.description: Deliberately not an enum. The routes write several values for different notions of readiness, and publishing a guessed list is how a client comes to reject a state the server legitimately sends. `ready` is the one observed on a healthy base.

IntegrationCatalogItem.description: Available integration (connector) type in the catalog

id.description: Connector id (e.g. github, stripe, notion, slack)

OAuthCompleteRequest.description: Body to complete OAuth after callback

AuthVerifyCodeRequest.description: Body for POST /api/v1/auth/verify-code. No request_id; code is bound to email only.

code.description: OTP from email (6 digits); spaces are stripped server-side

AuthVerifyCodeResponse.description: Success response: API key to use as Bearer token

api_key.description: uarp_<prefix>_<secret>; store and use as Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

OAuthLoginProviderItem.description: Public-safe descriptor for an OAuth login (identity) provider. Surfaces only what the login page needs to decide which buttons to render — never exposes client_secret.

enabled.description: true when the operator has configured client_id+client_secret AND set enabled=true. False values mean clicking the button would 404.

OAuthLoginProviderConfigStatus.description: Admin view of one provider's current config. client_secret is never echoed; client_secret_hint shows the last 4 chars so the operator can confirm storage.

configured.description: false when no record exists yet; remaining fields are absent in that case

client_secret_hint.description: Masked tail of the stored secret (e.g. "••••a1b2"). null if no secret on file.

scopes.description: null when no override; provider defaults apply

OAuthLoginProviderConfigUpdate.description: Body for PUT /api/v1/admin/oauth-login-providers/{provider}. Merges with existing record: an operator flipping `enabled` or rotating `scopes` does not need to re-paste the secret. The first-time PUT (no existing record) requires both client_id and client_secret.

client_id.description: OAuth app client ID issued by the provider

client_secret.description: OAuth app client secret. Stored verbatim in admin KV; never echoed back.

enabled.description: Defaults to existing value, or true on first write if omitted

scopes.description: Optional override of the provider's default scope list. Omit to inherit defaults.

OAuthLoginProviderConfigUpdateResponse.description: Result after PUT — confirms the persisted state

OAuthLoginProviderConfigDeleted.description: Result after DELETE — record removed from admin KV

configured.description: Always false after a successful DELETE

BadRequest.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON, missing required header, or semantically rejected before validation.

Forbidden.description: Insufficient permissions, missing scope, suspended tenant, quota exceeded, or governance/emergency-mode block.

NotFound.description: Resource does not exist or is not visible to this tenant.

Conflict.description: State conflict (duplicate, already exists, version mismatch). Idempotency-Key collisions return 202 with Retry-After, not 409.

Gone.description: Resource was permanently removed (e.g. terminated agent, expired share link).

LengthRequired.description: Content-Length header required for application/json requests

ServiceUnavailable.description: Backend dependency unavailable, emergency mode active, or queue saturated. Retry with backoff.

OpenAiBadRequest.description: The request was rejected. `error.message` says why.

OpenAiNotFound.description: No such agent or response id.

OpenAiNotImplemented.description: The capability is not enabled on this deployment — a permanent configuration state, not an outage. Do NOT retry: only an operator change can resolve it. `error.code` names the missing capability (e.g. `embedding_unavailable`) and `error.message` says where to enable it.

OpenAiServiceUnavailable.description: The configured upstream provider failed to answer. Genuinely transient — retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

InternalServerError.description: Unhandled server error. The `correlationId` field on the response body is the request ID for support escalation.

IdempotencyInFlight.description: An identical request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is currently in-flight. Retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Unique key for idempotent request. Duplicate requests with the same key within 24 h return the cached response with header `X-Idempotency-Replayed: true`. In-flight collisions return `202 + Retry-After`.

SseToken.name: token
SseToken.description: Short-lived SSE/WebSocket token (mint via `POST /api/v1/auth/sse-tokens`) or full API key. Used by browser EventSource which cannot set Authorization header.

LastEventId.name: Last-Event-ID
LastEventId.description: SSE resumption cursor. The browser's EventSource sets this automatically on reconnect; servers replay events strictly after this id.

XIdempotencyReplayed.description: Set to `true` on responses that replayed a cached idempotent result rather than executing the handler.

pending_resumes.description: Runs waiting to be resumed after a restart.

200.description: Server is ready to accept requests

post.x-auth-note: One-time install bootstrap. Answers 401 once a tenant exists — an API key cannot re-run it, by design.

200.description: Cursor-paginated session list. Items are enriched with `agent_name`, `first_user_message`, `last_message`, `message_count`.

model_override.description: Per-conversation model override. Send null to clear (revert to agent default), or { provider, model_ref, endpoint_url?, capabilities? } to set. The runtime governance allowlist is still enforced at run time.

post.description: Submits a user message to the session and schedules a run on the bound agent. Returns `202 Accepted` with the new run id; subscribe to `/api/v1/runs/{runId}/events` (SSE) for streaming output.

command.description: Optional slash-command string when the message is a builtin command.

file_ids.description: Optional attached file ids previously uploaded via /api/v1/files.

workspace_id.description: Workspace override for this message; defaults to the agent's workspace.

200.description: SSE event stream of session events.

schema.description: Server-Sent Events. Each event has fields `id`, `event`, `data` (JSON-encoded payload).

404.description: No share link for this session

post.description: Creates a run and schedules it for execution. Recommended: send Idempotency-Key header to avoid duplicate runs on retries; a repeated request with the same key returns the cached 202 response (same run_id). Pin a specific agent version with `version` to bypass the head pointer.

version.description: Pin to a specific agent version (1-based). When omitted, runs against the agent's current head version.

409.description: Conflict: session has queue_mode reject and already has an active run (queued, running, or paused)

get.description: Returns the ordered list of steps executed during a run, with per-step metrics including tokens, cost, and tool calls.

Real-time event stream for a run. Supports `Last-Event-ID` header (or `?last_event_id=`) for reconnection. Stream closes when run reaches terminal status. Each event payload includes `stream_type`: lifecycle (run.*), assistant (llm.chunk), tool (tool.*), or other — use it to filter client-side. Browsers using EventSource (which cannot set Authorization headers) should mint a 60-s SSE token via `POST /api/v1/auth/sse-tokens` and pass it as `?token=`.

get.summary: List recent memories for an agent

post.summary: Ingest a file into agent memory
post.description: Chunks the file content (default 600 chars), embeds each chunk, and stores embeddings as memory entries. Source: pre-uploaded `file_id` (preferred) or inline `content`. Max 2 MB of text per ingest call; rate-limited and quota-counted.

content.description: Inline text body when no file_id is provided. Max 2 MB.

filename.description: Override stored filename; defaults to file metadata or `created-doc.md`.

get.summary: Get memory entries associated with an entity

post.description: Creates an experiment to compare evaluation results across multiple agent versions.

autonomous_mode.description: When true, schedule is fired by autonomous tick with reflection prompt instead of cron run with input.

reflection_prompt.description: Prompt injected into run input when autonomous_mode is true (e.g. review pending work, plan next steps).

200.description: Schedule details, or null in response body when no schedule is set

get.description: Returns the calling tenant's profile. Any authenticated key passes — no scope required.

Rollback an agent to a previous version

post.x-auth-note: Authenticated by Stripe's HMAC signature (`Stripe-Signature`), not by a bearer token. A tenant API key is rejected with 401.
post.description: Processes incoming Stripe events (invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.deleted). Bypasses normal auth — `Stripe-Signature` header is HMAC-verified against the webhook signing secret.

parameters.name: Stripe-Signature
parameters.description: Stripe webhook signature in `t=<timestamp>,v1=<sig>` format. Required; missing or invalid signatures are rejected with 400.

post.summary: Continue a run from a continuation token
post.description: Decodes the token, loads the checkpoint, and re-schedules the run.

queue_position.description: 0 means not in queue or currently running

get.summary: Wait for run to reach terminal status
get.description: If the run is already completed, failed, cancelled, timeout, or guardrail_blocked, returns 200 with the run immediately. Otherwise polls until terminal status or timeout_sec. On timeout returns 202 with status still_running.

parameters.name: timeout_sec
parameters.description: Max seconds to wait. Default from server config (e.g. 60).

202.description: Timeout reached while run still in progress

post.description: The body is optional; sending none approves without a message. `reject` has always taken a body, and the asymmetry was an omission rather than a design.

get.summary: Get the calling user + tenant context
get.description: Single source of truth for the browser to render account state, role badges, and the tenant header. Resolves the user via api-key.user_id, then JWT `sub` claim, then tenant_primary_email lookup.

get.summary: List OAuth identity providers (for login UI)
get.description: Public, IP-rate-limited (60/min). Returns the list of configured OAuth login providers with their enabled status — UI uses this to render only the buttons that will work. `apple` is always advertised as enabled (App Store Guideline 4.8 placement requirement); `github`/`google` enabled depends on whether super-admin has provisioned client_id+client_secret.

post.summary: Trade a mobile hand-off code for the session
post.description: Second half of the mobile sign-in hand-off. When `start` is called with `app_code_challenge`, the callback redirects to the app with `#code=` instead of `#api_key=`, and the key is only released here, to a caller that presents the matching verifier. Single-use and short-lived: the code is consumed on the first attempt, successful or not.

200.description: Session released to the app that started the flow

400.description: Code unknown, already used, expired, or the verifier does not match. Deliberately one message for all four — distinguishing them would tell a caller which half it got right.

get.summary: Begin browser OAuth login (302 to provider)
get.description: Redirects the browser to GitHub/Google authorize URL. Server stores a one-shot state record (10 min TTL) keyed by the `state` query the provider will echo back. PKCE codeVerifier is generated server-side. `return_to` defaults to nothing (response is JSON); when set, must satisfy the allow-list (same-origin paths, configured Universal-Link hosts, or `snaga://`). `device_label` is captured here and surfaces on the minted `api_key` for `/me/sessions`.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Where to redirect after callback. Same-origin paths, Universal-Link hosts (default `snaga.ai/auth/callback`), and `snaga://` allowed. Anything else is silently dropped.

parameters.name: device_label
parameters.description: Human-readable device name surfaced on the minted api_key.

get.summary: OAuth callback — exchange code, mint session
get.description: Provider redirects here. Server validates state (one-shot, 10 min TTL, provider-bound), exchanges `code` for tokens, fetches verified email + IdP `sub`, then mints a session via the shared post-verify path. On success: 302 to `${return_to}#api_key=...&email=...` if a return_to was stored, else JSON `{api_key, email}`. Refuses to mint for super-admin email (Guideline-style separation: super-admin must use OTP).

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Provider-side error (e.g. `access_denied`). When present, server returns 400.

200.description: Session minted (when no return_to was stored)

400.description: Missing code/state, expired/unknown state, provider mismatch, token exchange failed

403.description: Email not verified by provider, or super-admin email collision

502.description: Failed to fetch userinfo from provider after successful token exchange

post.summary: Sign in with Apple — native iOS handshake
post.description: iOS drives the Apple authorization sheet via `ASAuthorizationController` and POSTs the resulting `identity_token` (Apple-signed JWT, RS256) here. Server fetches Apple JWKS (cached 24h), verifies signature/iss/aud/exp, extracts `sub` + `email`, then mints a session. The `email` is only present on first login — subsequent logins reuse the stored `apple_sub_to_email` mapping. `is_private_email` (`@privaterelay.appleid.com`) is honoured: relay address is stored as the canonical email.

user.description: Apple's stable `userIdentifier` (informational only — server reads `sub` from the JWT).

name.description: User profile name from Apple. Apple supplies this only on first sign-in; iOS should cache it locally and resend if the user record needs to be bootstrapped.

**Scope dispatch is dynamic per JSON-RPC method**: read-style methods (`tasks/get`, `tasks/pushNotification/get`) require `agents:read`; write-style (`tasks/send`, `tasks/sendSubscribe`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/pushNotification/set`) require `agents:write`. get.description:
Entries visible to the calling tenant, newest first.

**Walking `prev_hash` across this page is NOT a verification, and treating it as one produces false alarms.** `seq` is global across all tenants while this list is scoped to one, so consecutive rows here are usually NOT consecutive in the ledger — the entry a row's `prev_hash` names belongs to another tenant and is not returned. Measured against production on 2026-08-20 over three independent samples: every pair whose `seq` values were adjacent chained correctly, and every pair with a gap did not — 10/10 and 0/5 in the last sample, while `GET /governance/ledger/verify` answered `valid: true` at the same moment.

A client that walks the chain of a page therefore reports tampering in a ledger the server certifies as intact. Integrity has an authority, and it is `GET /governance/ledger/verify`; a page-local walk can say "adjacent and chained" or "cannot be checked from here", never "broken".

total.description: Number of entries IN THIS RESPONSE, not the size of the ledger. Measured 2026-08-20: `total` was 16 while `GET /governance/ledger/verify` reported `entries_checked: 6698` against the same ledger a second later. Rendering this as "events recorded" understates the ledger by three orders of magnitude.
